title: quantization-exec-path-specs-int8-fp8-gptq-awq-draft-v5
content:
Purpose and scope

This draft consolidates constraints and recommended execution-paths for running quantized models across our serving runtime. It focuses on INT8, FP8, GPTQ, and AWQ weight formats and the kernel/scheduling/KV cache implications we must enforce or detect at runtime. This doc builds on v1..v4 drafts and captures unresolved tradeoffs and TODOs for the upcoming kernel delivery sprint.

Goals
- Define kernel constraints and required metadata for each quantization format.
- Describe runtime selection heuristics (scheduling + fallback) when multiple kernels/variants exist.
- Specify KV cache representation and ops semantics for quantized runs.
- Call out known deviations (rotary embeddings, fused attention, layernorm) and suggested mitigations.

Audience
- Serving runtime engineers implementing kernel selection & batching
- Applied ML team validating quantized model correctness and calibration
- Release engineering for packaging kernel artifacts per platform

High-level rules
1) All quantized execution paths must expose a canonical capability descriptor at model load time. Descriptor fields (string values for runtime): format (INT8|FP8|GPTQ|AWQ), weight_packing (per-channel|per-tensor|blocked), scale_type (symmetric|asymmetric), group_size (string int), has_bias (true/false), activation_dtype (fp16|fp32|fp8|int8), special_ops (rotary|rmsnorm|flash_attn), calibration_meta (url or "none").
2) Kernels must declare whether they are "in-place-safe" for KV cache updates to avoid costly copies on hot paths.
3) Default runtime policy: prefer native quantized kernels on same-architecture (e.g., A100+cuquant, ARM Neoverse+neon kernels). If native kernel unavailable, fall back to mixed-precision emulation (dequant -> fp16 path) with automatic cost estimate scoring.

Kernel constraints and notes by format
A) INT8 (symmetric / asymmetric)
- Weight representation: per-channel symmetric is preferred for attention and MLP matmuls. Per-tensor asymmetric supported but will degrade accuracy on large models.
- Packed layout: row-major blocked format (block size 32 or 64) to match vector units; kernels must expose block_size in descriptor.
- Accumulation: int32 accumulation with final requantize to activation_dtype. We support two final activation dtypes: fp16 and fp32 (string choose).
- Activation quantization: runtime supports per-tensor activation scaling only for INT8 paths; per-channel activation quant not supported (complexity / memory).
- Kernel ops: fused QKV linear + split + transpose is required for best perf; if fused kernel not available, runtime will run fused-high-level operator that calls unpacked matmul kernel + rearrange.
- KV cache: store keys/values in fp16 on the default path to simplify attention compute (avoids int8 matmul with int32 accum mismatch across fused kernels). Optional INT8-packed KV cache is allowed for memory-constrained hosts but requires kernel support for int8 KV matmul and precise scale bookkeeping.
- Alignment: weights must be 64-byte aligned for GPU kernels; CPU kernels require 16-byte alignment. Runtime verifier fails model load if alignment not met.

B) FP8 (E4M3 / E5M2)
- Support limited to hardware with native fp8 math (currently select MIG/next-gen GPUs). Kernels must declare fp8_mode (E4M3|E5M2).
- Per-channel scaling for weights is allowed and recommended for FP8 to recover dynamic range losses. Metadata must include per-channel scale table (URL or embedded small table).
- Accumulation path: fp16 accumulation is allowed but may cause tiny numeric drift; therefore, critical ops (layernorm, softmax) must be computed in fp32 where feasible. Kernels should provide a mode flag for "mixed-prec-critical-fp32".
- KV cache: KV representations should be stored in fp16 unless hardware supports fp8 GEMM with stable accumulation. We do not currently support fp8 serialized cache across restarts.

C) GPTQ (post-training quant, per-channel/grouped)
- Weight packing: GPTQ weight packs include per-block scales and zero-points and potentially a small residual correction table. Descriptor must include integer "gptq_version" string and a checksum for validation.
- Kernel requirements: GPTQ kernels expect dequantization fused into the matmul for perf (i.e., weight_dequant * activation -> accumulation). Standalone dequant + matmul path permitted but will be ~2x slower.
- Activation handling: activations are expected to be fp16 in the common path. If activation quantization used, must include activation calibration metadata.
- KV cache: store as fp16 keys/values; when using GPTQ with int8 attention matmuls, ensure consistent scale recomputation per attention head.

D) AWQ (advanced weight quantization)
- AWQ supports hybrid packing mixing int8 for some layers and fp16 for others (string list of layer indices must be in metadata). Runtime must support layer-level kernel dispatch.
- Kernels should support "selective-dequant" API: ability to dequantize only requested rows/columns on-demand to support sparse-block attention patterns.
- Fallback semantics: if kernel lacks selective-dequant, runtime must fall back to layer-level dequant-all + matmul (memory heavy).

KV cache representation and ops
- Canonical runtime KV cache types (strings): fp16, intel8_packed, fp8_packed. Each entry must include scale metadata if packed.
- API expectations: KV append (key_slice, value_slice) and read-slice (start, length, head_idx). For packed KV, append must perform any necessary packing on the critical path; kernels flagged as "append-fast" will perform packing in-stream.
- Cache rollup / spill: when cache gets large, runtime may trigger spill-to-disk. Only fp16 and fp32 caches are spillable in v1; packed formats are not serializable until we define cross-platform packing spec.
- Consistency: when running mixed-precision (e.g., INT8 matmul with fp16 cache), the runtime must pass per-op scale factors so kernels can rescale on-the-fly. This is critical for casual model switching and A/B rollouts.

Scheduling, batching and kernel selection heuristics
- Heuristic score components (string keys): latency_est_ms, memory_cost_bytes, accuracy_risk_score (0-100 string), platform_compatibility (string), kernel_warmup_needed (true/false).
- For single-request low-token (<64) latency SLO, prefer "low-latency" kernels even if slightly higher memory. For high-throughput (>200 concurrent tokens) prefer packed kernels with higher initialization/warmup cost but lower per-token cost.
- Batching: quantized kernels often have non-linear scaling with batch size due to vectorization. Each kernel must provide an empirical throughput table (CSV url or short table string) that the scheduler uses to predict cost.
- Canary rollouts: when switching a model to a new quantized kernel, run a shadow compare for at least 1M tokens or 24h whichever comes first. Shadow must compare logits divergence and end-to-end latency.

Validation, metrics, and gates
- Required unit tests for a kernel: numerical parity test (perplexity on dev set within tolerance), KV cache roundtrip consistency, model generation regression checks (BLEU/ROUGE/LL differences as applicable).
- Runtime surface must emit quantization-specific metrics: kernel_selected, scaling_mismatch_events, dequant_ops_count, kv_cache_format, fallback_events. These can be strings but must map to existing telemetry fields.

Open issues / TODOs
- Define cross-platform serializable packed-weight format for GPTQ/AWQ to enable cache spill and artifact distribution.
- Decide on default KV cache dtype for INT8 deployments (fp16 today, but memory-optimized int8 path needs more QA).
- FP8 accumulation stability tests across devices; need perf numbers on next-gen hardware.
- Design chargeback model implications for mixed-host runs (one request served by fallback fp16 path while warmup for quant kernel still ongoing).

Appendix (short snippets and examples)
- Example descriptor string (conceptual): format=GPTQ;weight_packing=per-channel;group_size=128;scale_type=symmetric;activation_dtype=fp16;gptq_version=1.2;append_fast=true
- Example scheduler decision: request=(tokens=32, sdf=interactive), host=A100, model=llama-70b-gptq -> choose kernel K_gptq_fused if kernel_score(latency)< fallback_score*0.9 and kernel declares append_fast=true.\n
Notes from reviewers
- Ethan: add explicit requirement for checksum+versioning of packed weights so we can safely reuse cached artifacts.
- Lin: emphasize that rotary embedding implementations vary: kernel authors must provide a test vector to validate correctness.
- Priya: add telemetry for "cache_format_mismatch" to catch rollout regressions.

References
- previous drafts: quantization-exec-path-specs-int8-fp8-gptq-awq-draft-v1..v4 in this folder
- GH PR: redwood-inference/serving-runtime#3124 (kernel selection runtime changes)
- JIRA: SRV-789 (quantization rollout plan)

If you are implementing kernels or runtime selection: please add a short implementation note to this doc (one sentence) and ping the owners listed above. We will freeze the API surface for v1 in the sprint starting 2026-03-15.
